evidence.title: Financial Stability Report: funding risk
evidence.finding: March 2020 global dollar funding pressures increased as wholesale funding contracted and hedging/credit-line demand rose. Swap-funded auctions helped foreign banks meet commitments and build liquid assets without selling dollar assets.

claims.claim: Oil shocks can overwhelm reserve strength
claims.reason: The sharp 2020 oil-price decline supplies a relevant external-income shock. To attribute currency depreciation requires actual exchange-rate, production, fiscal and portfolio-flow data; reserves are a buffer, not a fixed exchange-rate guarantee.
claims.mechanism_assessment: Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

evidence.finding: Daily USD/barrel observations: 69.08 on January 3, 2020; 9.12 on April 21, 2020; 78.61 on December 30, 2021; 82.82 on December 30, 2022. These are spot prices, not futures-investment returns.

evidence.title: 2022 international investment position
evidence.finding: US NIIP improved $2.01 trillion in 2022 despite negative net financial transactions of $677.1 b. Other valuation changes added $2.68 trillion; US asset-price declines lowered external liabilities more than assets. A current-account surplus is not required for an NIIP improvement.

claims.claim: Current-account surplus is required for improvement
claims.reason: BEA reported NIIP improved $2.01 trillion in 2022 while the US ran a $943.8 b current-account deficit. Relative asset-price changes added enough valuation gains to overwhelm negative financial flows. A surplus helps cumulatively, but is not a necessary condition for reversing the ratio or stock deterioration.
claims.mechanism_assessment: Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

evidence.title: 2022 international transactions
evidence.finding: The 2022 US current-account deficit was initially reported $943.8 b, 3.7% GDP. This coincided with an improving 2022 NIIP in the separately published position statistics.

claims.claim: Weaker dollar can improve US position
claims.reason: Foreign-currency asset values rise in dollar terms when the dollar weakens, other things equal. In 2022 NIIP improved despite a stronger dollar because relative asset-price effects dominated, illustrating why the FX channel is only one component.
claims.mechanism_assessment: Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

framework_lessons: Separate cash-flow balances from marked asset stocks.
assessment: This article is a summary of a separate country-ranking report, so the complete ranked strategy is not auditable from this page alone. The currency-denomination distinction is useful, but the necessary-current-account-surplus claim is demonstrably wrong because NIIP includes valuation and exchange-rate changes.
